name: CR-Int-16-trigonometric-5
questiontext: Find \[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}. \] Hint: Use a trigonometric identity and note that the derivative of \(\tan(t)\) is \(\sec^2(t)\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: For this question we need to use the identity \[tan^2(A) = sec^2(A) - 1\] as follows: \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}}\] So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:3}} d{{CT:1}} + \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} \end{array}\]
